children: Crude futures settle lower after President Trump waived some new sanctions against Russia, with downside limited by continuing conflict in the Middle East keeping supply risks high. Much of the selling looked technical as Friday's late-session advance "looked mismatched against fresh headlines," Ritterbusch & Associates says in a note. December Brent settles down 0.3% at $109.55 a barrel, and December WTI falls 0.5% to $98.54. WTI for November rose 2.2% to $103.66 a barrel ahead of Tuesday's contract expiry. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
